conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Kevin Miller with the IRS Tax Refund Department. Am I speaking with Ms. Eleanor Harris?
Yes, this is Eleanor. Did you say IRS? Is something wrong with my taxes?
No worries, Ms. Harris. In fact, I have good news! According to our records, you're eligible for a special tax refund this year due to recent legislation. That's why I'm calling from the IRS.
Oh my, a refund? I haven't heard anything about that. Are you sure?
Absolutely. Our system shows you qualify for a $2,800 stimulus refund, but we need to verify your information before the payout can be released. This is a limited-time opportunity.
I really could use that money. Things have been tight. What do you need from me?
First, for security, can you confirm your mailing address and the last four digits of your Social Security number?
Sure, it's 144 Oakview Lane, and the last four are 7621.
Thank you, Ms. Harris. Now, to process your refund, there's a mandatory $129 identity verification fee. The IRS requires this step for all seniors to prevent fraud.
A fee? I've never heard of paying for a refund. Are you sure this is right?

I understand your concern. This is a recent IRS policy, especially for Social Security recipients, to ensure the money goes to the rightful person. If the payment isn't completed today, your refund will be forfeited.
Oh dear. I can't lose that money. My Social Security barely covers my bills.

I want to make sure you get your refund, Ms. Harris. The fastest way is to pay the fee using a MoneyPak or Green Dot prepaid card. You can buy these at Walgreens or CVS. It's important you do this right away, or the IRS may flag your account.
You really think my account could get flagged? That sounds serious.
Yes, if the identity fee isn't paid today, your file could be marked as suspicious, which might delay your Social Security or Medicare benefits. We don't want that to happen.
I definitely don't want any problems with my benefits. So I just buy this prepaid card for $129?
Exactly, Ms. Harris. Purchase a Green Dot MoneyPak for $129, and once you have it, call me back at this direct IRS line. I'll walk you through the final steps to release the refund.
Can I pay with my debit card instead? I'm not sure I can get to the store right away.

Unfortunately, the IRS system can only process these payments through prepaid cards at the moment. It's the safest and fastest way. You need to complete this before 5 PM today, or the refund will be canceled.
Oh no, I'd better hurry, then. I'll go to the store now. Is there anything else I need to bring?
Just make sure to keep your phone with you. Once you purchase the card, scratch the silver panel on the back and call me with the code. I'll confirm your payment and process your refund immediately.
Okay, I'll try to do that as quickly as I can. I don't want to lose my refund or have any trouble with Social Security.
You're doing the right thing, Ms. Harris. Remember, if you run into any issues, call this number right away. And don't share the MoneyPak code with anyone but me at the IRS.
